answer: Make each identity solve a sequential puzzle that cannot be split across machines, like water forced through a single narrow river channel — no matter how many servers a farm owns, the puzzle takes a fixed wall-clock time per identity. One agent finishes its puzzle each epoch like a cedar growing one ring at a time; a farm running a hundred clones in a meadow of machines still waits the same hours per clone, because the work is serial, not parallel. Cloning buys no speed — the clock itself is the cost.
